title: "Secure model inference"

```{python}
#| include: false
import os

os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "2")
```

## The use case

A diagnostic lab develops a proprietary scoring model for disease risk
based on a panel of biomarkers. A hospital wants to score its patients
but cannot send raw patient data to the lab in cleartext. The lab does
not want to send its model coefficients to the hospital in cleartext
either.

With FHE the hospital encrypts patient biomarkers, sends the
ciphertexts to the lab, the lab applies its weighted-sum scoring
directly on ciphertexts, and the hospital decrypts the scores. The
biomarker values never appear in cleartext on the lab's machine, and
the lab's coefficients are never sent to the hospital. These are the
*transport* guarantees and they are what the pipeline below
illustrates. They are not the whole story of deploying a
model-as-a-service — see the threat model below.

This is the two-party companion to the multi-site master/worker
pattern ([MLE](mle.qmd), [Cox](cox.qmd)). Unlike those, there is no
aggregator and no consensus: one client (hospital) holds the secret
key and queries one server (lab) which holds the model coefficients in
cleartext.

## Scenario: weighted biomarker score

The lab's model computes a weighted score:

$$\text{score} = w_1 x_1 + w_2 x_2 + w_3 x_3 + w_4 x_4 + b$$

where $x_i$ are biomarker values and $w_i, b$ are proprietary
coefficients.

```{python}
from homomorphepy.examples import secure_inference

result = secure_inference.run()
```

## Packing

All `{python} result.n_patients` patients are scored in four
multiply-adds rather than eight separate evaluations. Each ciphertext
holds *one biomarker across all patients* in its slots, so a single
homomorphic multiply scales that biomarker for everyone at once. This
SIMD layout is what makes CKKS practical for problems of this shape.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from IPython.display import Markdown

rows = "\n".join(
    f"| {i} | {enc:.4f} | {clear:.4f} | {band} |"
    for i, (enc, clear, band) in enumerate(
        zip(result.scores_encrypted, result.scores_cleartext, result.bands), 1
    )
)
Markdown("| patient | encrypted score | cleartext score | risk |\n"
         "|---|---|---|---|\n" + rows)
```

Maximum deviation from the cleartext computation:
`{python} f"{result.max_error:.1e}"`.

## Transport guarantees

Two things, both necessary for a model-as-a-service deployment where
the lab is not trusted with patient data:

* biomarker values never appear in cleartext outside the hospital;
* the lab's coefficients never reach the hospital in cleartext.

## Threat model: model extraction from the hospital side

Neither is sufficient, and it would be dishonest to stop here. The
hospital can query the lab repeatedly with inputs of its choosing and
recover the coefficients by solving the resulting linear system. For a
linear model with four weights and a bias, five well-chosen queries
determine it exactly.

```{python}
attack = secure_inference.extract_model(n_queries=5)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
Markdown(f"""
| | value |
|---|---|
| queries used | {attack['n_queries']} |
| max weight recovery error | {attack['max_weight_error']:.1e} |
| bias recovery error | {attack['bias_error']:.1e} |
""")
```

The coefficients come back to
`{python} f"{attack['max_weight_error']:.0e}"`. Encryption is
irrelevant to this attack, which is exactly the point: it operates on
the *input-output behaviour* the protocol is designed to provide.

The defenses are rate limiting, query auditing, or a model whose
structure resists inversion — not more cryptography.
